sections.heading: You saved it for later. Now where is it?
callsToAction: See the four ways to tidy
sections.text: BOOKMARK ORGANIZER FOR CHROME You saved it for later. Now where is it? The recipe from last spring, the hotel you almost booked, the article you meant to finish. Tidymark reads each page and files it where it belongs, so you can find it again. Save the page you're on with one click, or sort years of loose bookmarks in one pass. Add to Chrome See the four ways to tidy Works with the folders you already have. Nothing moves until you press Apply. Weeknight lasagna Running shoes review 3 days in Lisbon Easy weeknight lasagna a food blog SUGGESTED FOLDERS DinnersBEST Recipes 94% Recipes Bookmarks b

sections.heading: One click and it picks the folder.
sections.text: IN THE TOOLBAR One click and it picks the folder. Open the popup on any page. Tidymark reads the title, the address and the page description, then ranks your existing folders by how well they fit. Your three best folders, with a confidence score Tap one to save. The button tells you exactly where the bookmark will land. It won't force a bad fit When nothing scores high enough, it suggests a new folder, named after the site and placed next to the closest match. No duplicates Already saved that address? Tidymark moves the existing bookmark instead of making a second one. Auto-save if you want it

sections.heading: Sorted by the day you last opened it.
sections.text: MODE C IN DETAIL Sorted by the day you last opened it. Chrome remembers when you last used each bookmark. Tidymark turns that into four shelves. Anything saved in the last 14 days stays where it is. Optionally add the last 90 days of browsing history for better accuracy. History stays in your browser. Active opened in the last 30 days 358 Occasional opened 30–180 days ago 475 Someday saved, never opened 252 Archive not opened in 180+ days 353

sections.heading: Find what to delete, and what to put away.
sections.text: CHECKUP Find what to delete, and what to put away. 37 Broken links Pages that return 404 or 410, or whose domain is gone. Logins and temporary errors are left alone. DELETE 62 Duplicates Same address, ignoring #, trailing slashes, www. and utm_ tags. Keeps the one that's filed or recently used. DELETE 11 Empty folders Folders with nothing inside. DELETE 13 Stale folders Not changed or opened in a period you pick, from 6 months to 5 years. MOVE TO ARCHIVE Numbers are from an example library. Deleted bookmarks come back if you undo.

sections.heading: See what your bookmarks say about you.
sections.text: INTEREST REPORT See what your bookmarks say about you. Maybe it's 30% cooking, 20% travel plans and a surprising amount of houseplants. Tidymark reads every bookmark's title and description, maps out the topics you care about and how much of your library each takes up, then proposes a folder structure to match. One click sends that structure to mode A.

sections.heading: Nothing changes until you apply.
sections.text: BEFORE ANYTHING MOVES Nothing changes until you apply. You get a move plan grouped by destination. Change any row, untick what you don't like. Low-confidence rows are flagged for review and left unticked. And the last tidy can always be undone. One-bowl banana bread → Recipes / Baking Toddler sleep schedule by age → Family / Kids Standing desks compared → Shopping / Home office Untitled Review · 41% Apply 3 moves Undo last tidy

sections.heading: What leaves your browser.
sections.text: PRIVACY What leaves your browser. Last updated September 25, 2026 Read the full privacy policy → Where classification happens Tidymark sends pages to the Tidymark server for classification. It runs on Google Cloud Run in Seoul, South Korea. You can instead run your own server and point the extension at it in Settings; Chrome asks for your permission before the extension can reach a new address. What is sent For each bookmark or page being classified: its title, address, and page description (or text you have selected on the page). For folder matching, the names of your folders.
